newsitem.title: USA: Hot dog sales should rise with baseball attendance.
newsitem.headline: Hot dog sales should rise with baseball attendance.

text.p: While baseball fans chart hits, runs and errors, food vendors inside and outside ball parks this year expect to score a home run in hot dog sales.

With Major League Baseball estimating a nearly nine percent rise in attendance in 1997 to 65.37 million, "One would expect hot dog consumption would be up as well," Peter Marigliano, spokesman for the National Hot Dog and Sausage Council, said Wednesday.

Inside ivy-covered Wrigley Field, 10 to 15 percent more hot dogs should be consumed by Chicago Cubs fans, said Curt Radle, general manager of Ogden Entertainment, which supplies hot dogs, pretzels, peanuts and other foods to the park.

The New York Mets estimate 35,000 hot dogs will be consumed by opening day fans on April 12, about 10,000 more than opening day 1996, said Debbie Albert, spokeswoman for ARAMARK Managed Services, which provides food services to many major league baseball parks.

Baseball is big business for food vendors. Last year the council estimated 26 million hot dogs were consumed at Major League Baseball stadiums. The strike-shortened 1994 and 1995 seasons cut attendance to about 50 million each season. Fans are slowly returning, but 1997 attendance will probably fall short of the record 70.26 million in the 1993 season.
Many fans do not even wait until they get into the park for that first hot dog. Vienna Beef's Bob Schwartz said the big sales are outside the park, where people line up before game time.

"At the beginning of baseball season, when you open the doors, there is 20 percent more business done almost immediately," Schwartz said. Vienna Beef sells hot dogs, Polish sausages and bratwurst around Chicago's Comisky Park, home of the White Sox, and Wrigley Field.
Although other foods are competing for the baseball's fans dollars, the hot dog remains king.
"In all those parks, hot dogs are still king," said Tim Lawler, a regional vice president for ARAMARK. "That is the biggest selling meat item. The other is bratwurst."

Competitors include pizzas, soft pretzels and hamburgers. Some geographic favorites include bratwurst at Milwaukee's County Stadium, crabcakes at Baltimore's Camden Yards and Rocky Mountain oysters at the Colorado Rockies' Coors Field.
